newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares stumble lower, downward drift seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares stumble lower, downward drift seen.

text.p: Lack of follow through buying sent Singapore shares lower at the close on Wednesday. Dealers said they expected the market to drift lower the rest of the week as they did not foresee any significant event to lift share prices.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index lost 8.80 points to 2,162.89. Market turnover stayed thin at 72.43 million shares with losers edging out gainers by 176 to 130.
"The index is neither here nor there. A good level to start buying would be at the 2,100 level," said a dealer at a Japanese broking house.
"Second board stocks sort of perked up yesterday for a while but they seem to have died out," he said.

Interest centred on a few selected stocks. Among them were engineering group Van der Horst which attracted buying in anticipation of more deals after it announced a toll road project. It rose Singapore $0.50 to S$5.90 (US$4.18).

Jardine Matheson led the actives with nearly 3.0 million shares and fell US$0.15 to $5.75 after the group said it expected its profit to slump in 1996. Dairy Farm, part of the Jardine group was also active with 2.55 million shares and eased US$0.015 to $0.585.
